# Where AI might plug in

## A neural network as a component?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
- Universal differential equations and physics-informed networks pair
  a network with a mechanistic model. Here the renewal process is the
  mechanism
- A network in the $R_t$ slot learns what the AR process cannot say.
  Behaviour, season, policy
- A network on the observation side fits several data streams from the
  same latent infections
- No neural network code in any EpiAware package yet

::: {.attribution}
Rackauckas et al. 2020,
[arXiv:2001.04385](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.04385) ·
Millevoi, Pasetto and Ferronato 2024, PLoS Comput Biol ·
Philipps, Schmid and Hasenauer 2025, npj Syst Biol Appl ·
grep of the EpiAware organisation for Lux and Flux, 2026-09-11
:::
:::
::: {.column width="58%"}
![](../figures/exchange-nn-component.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Three boxes in a row: an infection model, Renewal with an
empty rt slot, an observation model of LatentDelay, Ascertainment and
NegativeBinomialError, and cases. Two candidates point at the R_t slot:
an AR process, labelled today, and a small neural network of
covariates, labelled a question, with a swap arrow between them. Under
the observation model a third candidate, a network from the latent
infections to cases, deaths and wastewater at once."}

## Renewal as a neural network layer

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Flux and Lux build models by stacking layers. The renewal equation is
  a convolution. A convolution is a layer
- Delays, ascertainment and the likelihood are layers too. The stack is
  composable by construction, inside the deep learning toolchain
- Pervez et al. write mechanistic models this way
- Priors and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo on one side, gradient training on
  the other. The same layers

::: {.attribution}
Pervez, Locatello and Gavves 2024,
[arXiv:2402.13077](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.13077) · Innes 2018,
[Flux.jl](https://fluxml.ai/) · the 2026 Wellcome Discovery application
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/exchange-renewal-layer.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="On the left the renewal equation, I_t equals R_t times the sum
over s of I_{t minus s} g_s, described as a convolution with a fixed
kernel scaled by R_t. On the right a stack of six layers: inputs, an R_t
layer marked learned, then a renewal layer, a delay layer and an
ascertainment layer marked fixed by the epidemiology, then a negative
binomial likelihood on cases."}

::: {.attribution}
Drawn for this talk, `scripts/exchange-schematics.py`
:::
:::

## An outbreak-specific foundation model

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Time series foundation models forecast well a few weeks out on sparse
  data. Less well at peaks and turning points
- CAPE pretrains on simulated compartmental epidemics. A model of
  outbreaks, but of the final curves
- Outbreak data change after the fact. On the DRC model the daily
  suspected stream stopped on 6 August, and in May INSP reclassified
  suspected cases
- A model pretrained on data as it was seen at the time, vintage by
  vintage. A project I would like to be part of

::: {.attribution}
Kalahasti et al. 2025, medRxiv · Wang, Li and Perra 2026, medRxiv ·
Jafari et al. 2026, [arXiv:2606.19560](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19560)
· Liu et al. 2026, CAPE, KDD · PNAS 2026,
[doi:10.1073/pnas.2526192123](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2526192123) ·
[BVDOutbreakSize][bvd] `README.md`
:::
:::
